newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Two sides on Cyprus welcome Holbrooke posting.
newsitem.headline: Two sides on Cyprus welcome Holbrooke posting.

text.p: Opposing sides on the divided island of Cyprus on Thursday welcomed the appointment of Richard Holbrooke as Washington's special envoy on the long-standing conflict.

"With the appointment of Richard Holbrooke as the new presidential emissary on Cyprus the government of the United States is implementing its promises and reaffirms the importance it places on a solution to the Cyprus problem," said Manolis Christofides, spokesman of the Greek Cypriot-led government of Cyprus.
Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash welcomed the appointment as a "positive step".
Holbrooke was assigned to his new post on Wednesday.
Denktash expressed confidence that Holbrooke's leading role in brokering the Bosnian peace agreement in 1995 would stand him in good stead in his new position.

"We hope he will quickly understand the realities of the Cyprus problem...and will present realistic reports to President Clinton," said Denktash, who heads a breakaway Turkish Cypriot administration recognised only by Turkey.
Denktash is due to meet Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides on July 9 in New York for U.N.-sponsored talks. It will be their first face-to-face encounter in nearly three years.
Christofides said the Cypriot government has received assurances of the "active, substantial and dynamic" presence of the United States on the sidelines of the New York talks.

Some 30,000 Turkish troops have been stationed in northern Cyprus since Turkey invaded the island in 1974 in response to a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.
In Ankara, Turkish officials said they welcomed every effort for a solution to Cyprus problem, but did not want to comment specifically on Holbrooke's appointment.
"Both sides on the island will themselves reach a solution," a foreign ministry official told Reuters. "We welcome every initiative that can contribute to the solution."
